definitions.name: upstream stream disconnection is an error, not a client cancellation
synchronous and asynchronous telemetry failures never interfere with successful inference
an upstream timeout after streaming begins reports an error rather than cancellation
cancellation during classification closes status without exposing a route or forwarding upstream

assertions.expression: assert.fail('Cancelled classification must not reach upstream')

assertion_order_scope: Raw successful assertion order retained separately. Per-site and per-callback counts are exact; no scheduling or chunk partition equivalence is inferred.
network_scope: Actual synthetic loopback HTTP only; the original injected routing callbacks remain supplied mocks; no evaluator calls.
capture_semantics: Complete selected callbacks and five helper statements restored unchanged except successful assertion-result wrappers. Recording delegates actual HTTP and original return objects; no clone/drain, substituted verdict, timing threshold or source clock changes. Per-peer complete bodies preserve actual parser-delivered bytes; raw push chunks and chronological reads remain in raw observations. Provider request bodies remain unread by the original callbacks. Actual stream failures and callback throws/rejections remain failures, with original Error objects delegated unchanged. The status callback Promise catch method is observed only when the original safe emitter installs and executes its own handler; the recorder never adds a detached rejection handler. Asynchronous assertions are counted only after their original Promise resolves successfully.
typed_observations: Headers inputs are enumerated into their complete normalized field map.
Route signal observation records actual AbortSignal type and aborted state; no serialized object identity is claimed. countTokens is recorded as a function capability only.
Individual response chunks remain base64, including intentionally split UTF-8. Only complete request bodies use UTF-8 after exact roundtrip validation.
